findings.text: Externally visible TDP helper resolves the terminal table position for one guest frame under direct roots for use by the shared fast fault path outside the main lock.
Externally visible TDP walk helper reports the root depth and captures the historical entry value observed at each traversed depth for one guest address.

Externally visible helper releases cached previous guest-mode roots, selecting entries whose backing page is absent or still marked for guest mode, and warns when invoked while guest mode remains active.
Externally visible helper discards previously cached roots that are flagged unsynchronized by freeing exactly that subset.

Externally visible generic asynchronous fault service admits a fault for background resolution, places a work item on the per-CPU queue, informs arch code, and hands the item to the system work service.
Externally visible arch hook records the faulting frame, attempts paravirtual notification to the guest, and otherwise asks the target CPU to enter a halt-like wait until the page becomes available.

Externally visible injector accounts a guest fault event and routes asynchronous faults that originated in nested guest state toward a nested exit, with all other cases delivered as a normal exception carrying code and payload.

Memory fault exits use a dedicated exit reason with address plus length describing one page, flags cleared except for an optional private marker when the fault concerns private state; direction is currently not encoded.

Paravirtual asynchronous notification communicates a not-present reason word through the guest-visible data area; failure to store that word prevents direct delivery and forces the halt-wait fallback.

The MMIO cache retains masked address, frame, access description and slot generation for later fault recognition, remains empty for nested paging translations, and refuses updates while a slot generation change is underway.

Cache recognition requires an exact generation match plus a non-zero stored value equal to the masked incoming address, uses frame comparison for direct translations and masked address comparison otherwise, and never matches for nested paging.

Fast handling excludes faults flagged for reserved bits and, on hosts with private memory, excludes cases where the fault privacy attribute disagrees with current bookkeeping; absent mappings are eligible only when global access tracking is disabled, while present mappings are eligible only for write accesses.

Permission evaluation treats absent entries as faulting, derives effective rights from present and write indicators combined with execution and user controls selected by active masking mode, narrows the fault code to write, user and fetch aspects, and consults the format permission matrix.

TDP fast lookup and walk operate on the direct root chosen by root type, with mirrored roots excluded from fast handling, and scan exactly one frame of address space while preserving the observed historical entry values.

Shadow chain inspection gathers the entry value at each depth from root to leaf inside a lockless window, delegating to the TDP variant when that mode is active and otherwise walking the legacy structures.

MMIO entry retrieval reports no reservation for an empty walk, bypasses reservation validation on a non-present terminal including intentionally reserved MMIO markers, aggregates reservation status across upper depths, and emits diagnostic hierarchy output when corruption is observed.

MMIO fault handling prefers cached recognition, rejects walks showing reservation corruption, and for validated MMIO markers refreshes the cache and requests emulation with direct addresses normalized, otherwise asks the guest to retry.
Write tracking interception applies only to present write faults without reservation flags whose frame is currently marked as write tracked.
Previous root maintenance frees only members selected by validity and mode or synchronization state, leaving currently valid synchronized entries retained.
Non-paging address translation clears any supplied exception code and resolves the input through the GPA translator with final-stage and full-access attributes.

Asynchronous fault identity combines a per-CPU incrementing sequence that avoids a zero shifted value with the CPU identifier, and arch setup pairs that identity with frame, code, mapping directness and either an invalid marker or current guest paging base.

Generic admission declines when the per-CPU outstanding count reaches its bound, when the host mapping is erroneous, or when backing storage cannot be obtained without waiting; otherwise it initializes a non-broadcast work item, queues it, updates the count, queries arch delivery, and schedules execution.
Arch delivery records the frame, traces the token with fault address, and on success injects a fault whose payload carries the token with zero code, else raises a halt-wait request without injection.

Injection accounting increments the guest fault counter, while nested asynchronous faults are queued as exits and other faults are queued as exceptions with code and address payload through a shared multi-exception path.

Outstanding asynchronous frames are remembered in a power-of-two table sized by the per-CPU bound, placed by hashing the low frame bits and advancing linearly modulo capacity until an empty sentinel is found.

Direct entry repair outside the main lock uses a single atomic compare exchange; a lost race leaves state unchanged, while a successful transition into writable state additionally marks the frame dirty in its slot.
Slot generation guards MMIO caching in both directions: caching is skipped during an update window and later recognition requires exact equality with the current generation.
Writable promotion of a large mapping is withheld from the fast path when its slot uses dirty tracking, deferring to the slow path so all constituent pages can be accounted.
Observed exit communication carries a reason field plus a nested fault record with address, length and flag word; only the private indicator is currently set from inputs.
Observed per-CPU MMIO state comprises masked address, frame number, access description and generation snapshot used jointly for later matching.

Observed fault description combines frame and address, present and reserved and write and execute and private attributes, slot reference and raw code used across eligibility, permission and repair decisions.
Observed asynchronous work carries owning CPU, fault address, host address, arch details, broadcast suppression, delivery outcome and queue linkage with a per-CPU outstanding count.

Fast fault resolution starts invalid, may become spurious when the current entry already allows the access, may become fixed after a successful atomic repair that changes permissions, otherwise remains invalid for absent or non-terminal or unfixable entries.

MMIO resolution yields emulation for cache hits and validated markers, a terminal error for reservation corruption, an invalid signal when validation fails, and retry when concurrent table release removed the mapping.
Asynchronous handling moves from admission to queued to arch notification to scheduled execution, with guest-visible outcome either an injected notification or a halt-wait request.
Guest fault injection serves as the arch entry for delivering both synchronous and paravirtual asynchronous faults with accounting and nested routing.
Generic asynchronous setup serves as the cross-arch entry for attempting background fault resolution with bounded per-CPU concurrency.
For protected guests a privacy mismatch misinterpreted as write protection would spin without progress, so such faults must avoid the fast path and receive explicit fault handling.
Concurrent table release can remove the terminal entry during lockless lookup; the fast path treats a missing pointer as frozen and the MMIO path treats a vanished mapping as retryable.
Reserved markers on present non-MMIO entries indicate table corruption, produce diagnostic output with full hierarchy, and must not be repaired as ordinary MMIO.
Repeated atomic repair races are bounded with a one-time diagnostic, after which the fault falls back to slower handling rather than looping indefinitely.
Exceeding per-CPU concurrency, erroneous host mappings, or allocation pressure cause silent decline of background handling so the caller must use the synchronous path.
Flooding mitigation clears write-flooding counters along the shadow chain for a supplied address while holding the lockless read window.
The TDP iteration construct confines traversal to a caller-supplied frame interval at the smallest page granularity.
The exception helper with payload forwards number, code validity, code and payload presence to the combined multiple-exception routine.

Fast repair, chain collection, MMIO inspection and flooding mitigation all execute their table reads inside paired lockless begin and end markers, with TDP fast lookup additionally converting a protected pointer for shared use under outside-lock contracts.
When global access and dirty support is disabled, fast handling restores tracked entries with an accessed indication before evaluating writability.
A per-CPU fast fault counter advances for any determinate fast outcome, and a guest fault counter advances on each injection.
Fast repair applies only to direct mappings where the frame identifier remains stable, excluding nested indirect structures.
